Visit note | 2025-12-24 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Hafsa Bepari, 48, female. Mrs. Bepari attends for review reporting persistent headaches upon waking and noting that a blood pressure check at a free health camp in Bashundhara showed a very high reading. She works as a garment merchandiser, lives in Dhaka, and reports no previous history of chronic illness or significant complaints. On examination: BP 169/107 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 83 kg. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are unremarkable. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check her blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-12-24 11:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Tushar Sarkar, 29, male. Mr. Sarkar returns for follow-up regarding facial blemishes, marks left after pimples, and blackheads on his face, which have worsened since working in a hot kitchen in Tangail. He has a known history of Bronchial asthma, which is currently stable. On examination: about 15 inflamed spots on the face, BP 135/82 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 94 kg. Skin shows scattered papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing the spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-12-24 11:30 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Arafat Mahmud, 30, male. Mr. Mahmud attends for a review of his gritty, burning eyes, which began after long gaming sessions at home in Cumilla involving extended screen time. He works as a photographer. He reports no other systemic complaints. On examination: tear break-up time 3 seconds, visual axes clear, BP 122/77 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 67 kg. Conjunctivae show mild dryness without acute infection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a room humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-24 12:30 PM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sabina Patwary, 27, female. Ms. Patwary presents for her first visit complaining of feeling slow and tired alongside noticeable weight gain, which she first observed when the cold winter weather in Uttara felt harder than usual. She works as an electrician and denies other medical conditions. On examination: TSH 12.4 mIU/L, BP 120/80 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 59 kg. Thyroid palpation is normal, and deep tendon reflexes show normal relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-12-24 12:30 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Mala Halder, 47, female. Mrs. Halder attends for review regarding her nasal symptoms, which have grown worse with dust exposure and a persistent runny nose since road construction began near her home in Narayanganj. She works as a delivery rider. She reports no other major medical illnesses. On examination: about 13 sneezing fits a day noted during consultation, nasal mucosa pale and boggy, BP 134/80 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 92 kg. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash her bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Afsana Awal, 50, female. Mrs. Awal comes for her first visit reporting burning pain during urination, going to the toilet frequently, and a dull lower belly ache that began during a hot week with little water intake in Faridpur. She works as a bank officer and has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: temperature 99.5°F, BP 136/75 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 60 kg. Suprapubic tenderness is present. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and avoid holding urine for long periods. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.

He works as a beautician and reports no chronic medical comorbidities. On examination: BP 174/95 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 60 kg. Heart sounds are normal and lung fields are clear. Visit note | 2025-12-24 04:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Farhan Akand, 62, male. Mr. Akand attends for review reporting morning stiffness lasting a few minutes and a creaking knee, which became worse after moving into a building with no lift in Old Dhaka. He works as a textile engineer and has no other reported systemic illnesses. On examination: BMI 32.2, BP 123/85 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 86 kg. Right knee shows mild crepitus and restricted terminal flexion with no significant effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Visit note | 2025-12-24 04:30 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Ruma Uddin, 78, female. Mrs. Uddin presents for her first visit with complaints of nausea accompanying a spinning sensation and brief episodes of spinning when turning over in bed, which began after she bumped her head on a rickshaw hood in Mohammadpur. She is a retired civil servant. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 83 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as demonstrated. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
